item.title: RT David States MD PhD: Ultrawide-bandgap materials like this AlGaO (>7 eV) suppress thermal carrier generation and can operate at temperatures far ab...
item.description:
RT David States MD PhD
Ultrawide-bandgap materials like this AlGaO (>7 eV) suppress thermal carrier generation and can operate at temperatures far above silicon limits—often 400–800°C in demonstrated Ga₂O₃, AlGaN, and AlN devices. Higher junction temperatures make waste heat more useful for recovery (better Carnot efficiency in thermoelectrics, TPV, or Rankine systems) while easing cooling needs in EVs, data centers, and high-power converters.
Cornell University: Cornell engineers have developed a semiconductor material with a record-setting bandgap and turned it into working devices, opening the door to electronics that handle much higher voltages while wasting less energy.

Read more: https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/11/cornell-semiconductor-sets-record-widest-bandgap.

item.title: RT Dr SurenMD: Re The diagnostic delay in rare disease is where families feel this gap most, often after years of referrals and fragmented records. An...
item.description:
RT Dr SurenMD
Re The diagnostic delay in rare disease is where families feel this gap most, often after years of referrals and fragmented records. An actionability report will be most useful if it separates established therapies from plausible but unproven options, and cites the evidence behind each one clearly. Clinicians also need a simple way to update the report when a new variant classification or trial result changes the picture. That audit trail matters if these reports are going to be trusted in clinic.

item.title: RT Eric Vallabh Minikel: How many times have you seen a mouse study claiming that a therapeutic works, and the survival curve looks like this? Broken ...
item.description:
RT Eric Vallabh Minikel
How many times have you seen a mouse study claiming that a therapeutic works, and the survival curve looks like this? Broken axis, 6% difference in survival time, but the P value is < 0.05 and it's claimed as a positive result. It's not. In my 15 years of prion science, I have learned to look past such claims almost instantly. Yet sometimes these claims still lead to high-profile publications, millions of dollars in funding, and even to therapies being tested clinically. In this new blog post I release data on 301 untreated control animals from our last 9 years of in vivo studies, model out the various ways that P values can appear significant even when the result is null, and put into words the intuition I've built up as to which claims are believable and which are not.

https://www.cureffi.org/2026/11/03/how-to-read-a-mouse-study/

item.title: RT Jay Bradner, M.D.: Jon Clardy was a brilliant scholar and a wonderful man, beloved uniformly in chemistry and chemical biology from Boston to Brazi...
item.description:
RT Jay Bradner, M.D.
Jon Clardy was a brilliant scholar and a wonderful man, beloved uniformly in chemistry and chemical biology from Boston to Brazil. My sincerest condolences to those who were lucky to know him well, as mentees and close friends. RIP, Jon, just cannot believe you are gone.
Michael Fischbach: Jon Clardy: 1943-2026
One of the most impactful, creative, and (quietly) irreverent practitioners of chemical biology. Transformed how we think about nature's chemicals: their structures, their role in biology. Loved him -- he had tremendous influence on my thinking.
